title: Choosing the focus of a practice
description: Before it starts you know where the guide directs attention; a session that does not suit you can be swapped.

blocks.text: The author of the review that follows is not suited by attention to the painful part of the body. Their complaint concerns the content of the exercise, not whether they are sitting or standing. One choice of posture does not solve this on its own.

quote.text: I love the breathing exercises but the body scanning is really really bad for someone suffering from chronic pain. I already focus too much on the part of my body that hurts naturally.

blocks.text: Explain the focus before the start

State clearly in the description where the author of the practice proposes to direct attention. Let people choose different content or end the session, keeping their own preferences without having to complete anything.
Do not substitute a prescription for a preference

This calls for work with authors and specialists in the field to describe the content and the limits of the material accurately. A personal review of an unpleasant experience does not prove the same reaction in everyone and does not set a universal substitute for an exercise.
